title: Open Space Commission Site Walk
location: Meet at Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: The Open Space Commission skips the conference room this month — members and the public will meet at Rebekah Hall on West Columbia at 4:00 PM, then head up Tomboy Road for a High Country site walk. No formal votes are on the agenda; this is a work session in the field, the kind of firsthand look that tends to inform decisions made later indoors.

title: Board of County Commissioners
location: BOCC Room, Ouray County Courthouse, 541 4th Street, Ouray, CO 81427
summary: A full day at the courthouse. The morning opens with consent items and a handful of proclamations before getting into substantive business: a Special Use Permit amendment for a restaurant in Colona, Ouray County's opt-in to Proposition 123's 2027-2029 affordable housing commitment cycle, a new intergovernmental agreement covering full law enforcement services between the county and the City of Ouray, and a veterans' medical transportation program with a new position request under the austerity resolution. The 2027 preliminary budget gets its public presentation at 10:45 — the first formal look at where the county's finances are headed next year. After lunch, the 2025 county audit is presented. The afternoon moves into two related public hearings before the Board of Adjustment and then the full BOCC sitting as itself: a variance application and an Exception application, both involving 13 applicants and 29 parcels in the Elk Meadows subdivision, seeking to ratify lot mergers that were recorded by deed but never formally approved by the county.

title: Special Town Council Budget
location: Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: A three-hour work session dedicated to the 2027 budget — specifically the enterprise funds, open space, affordable housing, and all remaining funds. No votes are on the table; this is the Town Council working through the numbers before formal adoption. Budget season in Telluride tends to surface the same underlying tensions: how much to spend on housing programs, how to sustain open space commitments, and how the enterprise funds — water, sewer, and the like — are holding up. Worth watching if you want to see where the priorities are before they get locked in.

title: Ouray Planning Commission Regular Meeting
location: Ouray Community Center, 320 6th Ave, Ouray, CO 81427
summary: One item drives this meeting: a proposed ordinance regulating natural medicine businesses in Ouray. Staff presenter Harper Powell brings two attachments — a clean draft ordinance and a supporting memo — suggesting this is still in the discussion phase rather than a vote. Colorado's legalization of natural medicine (psilocybin and related substances) under Proposition 122 left municipalities to figure out their own land-use and licensing frameworks, and Ouray is now working through what that looks like inside city limits. This is the kind of regulatory groundwork that tends to be quiet when it happens and consequential once it's done.

title: Norwood Water Commission Meeting
location: 1670 Naturita St, Norwood CO 81423
summary: A full agenda for the Norwood Water Commission's October 13 meeting. The biggest items center on the Cossey Complaint — the Commission will hold the hearing itself, consider a request to extend its date, and go into executive session twice for legal advice on that matter and separately on the Jubilee/Valentine Easement. Contract approval with Land Right and a review of SGM's Draft Environmental Assessment and Cultural Resources Report for the Redundant Line Project round out the infrastructure business. Four leak forgiveness requests are on the table for residential customers on Hwy 145, Summit St, Juniper, and Grand Ave. The Commission also takes up the 2027 Draft Budget and the 2025 Audit — both worth watching as water system costs continue to climb.

title: Board of County Commissioners Work Session
location: BOCC Room, Ouray County Courthouse, 541 4th Street, Ouray, CO 81427
summary: A full-day work session — no formal votes, but the direction set here tends to shape what comes next. The Ouray County Home Trust's Housing Services Administrator delivers a quarterly report, which means an update on where the county's affordable housing work actually stands. The Colorado River District gives its annual briefing, relevant given how water allocation questions shadow every land-use conversation in this region. Abram Herman presents on behalf of Friends of Youth and Nature. Midday shifts to County Manager performance feedback and commissioner reports. The afternoon gets substantive: Land Use takes up fee schedule updates — changes here affect what it costs to bring a development application — followed by a budget discussion with Ridgway Fire & EMS.

location: 5634 Cty Road H1, Egnar Fire Station, Egnar, CO 81325
summary: The Board of County Commissioners is holding a work session in Egnar — the far western end of San Miguel County, a long way from the box canyon in every sense. The posted agenda doesn't list specific items beyond the location itself, so there's no detail yet on what's being discussed. Worth watching for an agenda update if you track county business from the western slope side of things.

title: Ridgway Town Council Regular Meeting
summary: The Ridgway Workforce & Affordable Housing Committee meets the evening of October 14 — after the regular Council meeting — to take up two items from Home Trust of Ouray County. First, Housing Services Director Eva Henson delivers the Q3 2026 quarterly report: one year into the regional administrator arrangement, milestones include a rehabilitated rental unit returned to service at 835 2nd Street, the first deed-restriction resale at Riverfront Village (Unit 201, $395,000), and a $145,000 supplemental DOLA grant secured with no local match. The report also flags that Ridgway is expected to consider its Proposition 123 opt-in resolution at this same meeting, committing to add 13 deed-restricted units in the 2027–2029 cycle. Second, the committee will weigh whether to exercise the Town's Right of First Refusal on 683 Frederickson Street — a deed-restricted, two-bedroom/three-bath unit at the Wetterhorn Community with a maximum resale price of $429,659 — after Rural Homes, LLC declined to purchase. The Housing Services Administrator contract expires December 31, 2026; 2027 renewal planning is already underway.

title: Town Council Meeting
location: Town Hall, 455 Mountain Village Blvd, Suite A
summary: A full plate for the October 15 Council meeting. Two housing authority items come first in consequence: second reading of an ordinance amending MVHA fee language in the Municipal Code (Sections 16.01 & 16.02) to point to an annual fee schedule rather than hardcoded figures, paired with a resolution adopting the actual 2027 MVHA fee schedules — including Village Court Apartments rents. The gondola project surfaces again with a fourth supplement to the intergovernmental cost-sharing agreement for the 2027 planning and development budget. A three-party MOU between Mountain Village, San Miguel County, and the Ridge at Telluride HOA on the Ridge View Plane interpretation heads to a vote — view plane disputes in this canyon have a long history. Council will also consider a town manager employment agreement for Michael Bouchard, a work session on expanding the Munchkins childcare program, a draft Beaver Management Plan, a food truck CUP renewal, and a sustainable tourism services agreement with the Telluride Tourism Board. The meeting closes with an executive session on sewer authority negotiations with the Town of Telluride.

title: HARC Meeting
location: Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: The October 21 HARC meeting is anchored by the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment Project — the Town of Telluride's own large-scale development at 860 Black Bear Rd, zoned Accommodations 2. HARC takes up Buildings 1 and 2 as one public hearing item and Buildings 3 and 4 as a second, both continued from August 19. Each application covers new construction outside the Telluride Historic Landmark District exceeding 5,000 square feet of floor area under LUC 7-203.B.2.a.1. Also on the agenda: a payment-in-lieu of parking request for one space at 510 W Columbia Ave/129 N Townsend in the Historic Residential zone, where HARC is asked to support administrative approval. A small-scale new construction application at 785 Primrose Lane on a steep site is also up for review. The 448 Tomboy Road item has been continued to December 16 at the applicant's request, and the 214 S Fir Certificate of Appropriateness Amendment #2 — in the works since at least December 2025 — is being tabled for eight more months.
